analysis.investment_thesis: Carborundum Universal is a quality industrial abrasives and ceramics business with a nearly debt-free balance sheet, but at 74x P/E with ROE below 11% and a sharp FY2025 profit decline from ₹476 Cr to ₹299 Cr, I am paying a luxury price for a mediocre return. This is not my sector, and the numbers do not justify the valuation.
key_strengths: Fortress balance sheet with D/E of just 0.08 — management has been disciplined on debt
Revenue CAGR of 10.8% over 9 years shows steady, consistent compounding within my preferred range
Operating cash flow positive in all 5 of 5 years reviewed, indicating the business generates real cash
key_risks: Promoter holding of 38.9% is well below my 55% threshold — skin-in-the-game is insufficient
ROE of only 10.8% means management is not earning adequate returns on shareholder capital
Net profit collapsed from ₹476 Cr in FY2024 to ₹299 Cr in FY2025 — other income turned deeply negative at -₹23 Cr versus +₹118 Cr prior year, making earnings quality suspect
red_flags: P/E of 74.2x for a business earning 10.8% ROE — this is not a business I would pay even 25x for
Free cash flow nearly evaporated in FY2025 (₹28 Cr) despite ₹304 Cr operating cash flow, as capex consumed most of it
Low promoter ownership (38.9%) with no history shown of promoter buying — alignment with minority shareholders is questionable
Industrials/abrasives is outside my circle of competence — I do not understand end-market demand cycles well enough to have conviction
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Carborundum Universal is a well-run industrial company with virtually no debt, but that is where my enthusiasm ends. The P/E of 74.2x demands either exceptional ROE or exceptional growth — this business delivers neither, with ROE at a modest 10.8% and a 9-year revenue CAGR of 10.8% that, while steady, does not justify such a premium. The sudden collapse in net profit from ₹476 Cr to ₹299 Cr in FY2025, driven by a dramatic swing in other income from +₹118 Cr to -₹23 Cr, signals earnings that are not as clean and predictable as I require.

The promoter holding of 38.9% is a structural concern for me — I need promoters who have their entire lives tied to the business. With DIIs at 30% and FIIs at 11%, institutional holders are propping up the price, but they will exit the moment the growth story falters. Industrial abrasives is a cyclical business tied to manufacturing activity, which is not the predictable, consumer-facing demand profile I seek. I will wait on the sidelines unless the price corrects to 25-30x and the promoter demonstrates conviction by buying.
